Now:

That is a very important improvement.

This is currently the strongest engineering document in the package.

Why:

This alone increases enterprise credibility heavily.

- “engineering handoff capable specification”

Very important improvement:
- request/response structure
- validation boundaries
- deterministic payload expectations

This directly reduces:
- frontend/backend mismatch
- AI hallucinated APIs
- integration drift

# Excellent Strategic Addition

## `MendoraCI_MVPBuildLock`

This is VERY important.

Most hackathon teams fail because:
- scope mutates continuously
- AI keeps expanding architecture
- nobody freezes MVP

This document now acts as:
- delivery governor
- anti-feature-creep mechanism
- demo survivability layer

Good decision.

# User Stories Review

## `US001–US034`

Now much better.

The stories are:
- more implementation-ready
- more testable
- less abstract

But still missing in some areas:

### Missing

Need explicit:
- unhappy paths
- rollback scenarios
- timeout behaviors
- retry policies
- partial failure handling

Currently many stories still assume:
> “happy-path execution.”

Enterprise systems fail in:
- retries
- corrupted evidence
- webhook failures
- AI timeout states
- approval race conditions

Add those.

---

# Biggest Remaining Weakness

## Runtime Execution Flow

Still slightly under-modeled.

You describe:
- governance
- repair planning
- drift detection
- evidence

But runtime sequencing still needs:

### Missing

- orchestrator state transitions
- queue state model
- retry orchestration
- execution cancellation
- dead-letter queue behavior
- concurrency policy
- idempotency strategy

Without this:
developers will implement different runtime behaviors.

That creates:
- inconsistent evidence
- audit mismatch
- non-replayable actions

This is probably the biggest remaining enterprise gap.

---

# Compliance Review

Good correction.

The wording is now safer.

Before:
- too absolute
- dangerous guarantees

Now:
- more enterprise realistic
- lower legal exposure

Good:

- “governed recommendation”
- “confidence”
- “review required”

This matters for real buyers.

Good:
- realistic automation percentages
- practical CI thinking
- phased coverage strategy

Excellent improvement over:
> “100% everything”

Now feels achievable.

Still add:
- mutation testing policy
- flaky test quarantine policy
- golden dataset policy
- deterministic AI replay mode

Those matter for AI platforms.

---

# Competitor Appendix

Good addition.

But still weak in one area:

## Missing

Need explicit:
### “Why incumbents cannot easily absorb MendoraCI”

Currently competitor analysis mostly says:
- what they do
- where they differ

Need:
- moat logic
- operational gap proof
- why GitHub Copilot / Cursor / Devin / CI platforms don’t automatically kill this

That section is still missing.

---

# Most Important Missing Enterprise Artifact

You still need:

# Runtime State Machine Specification

This should include:

- queued
- validating
- planning
- repairing
- reviewing
- awaiting approval
- replaying
- failed
- rolled back
- archived

And transitions between them.

Without this:
the system is still partially conceptual.

This single document would dramatically improve implementation quality.

MendoraCI is now:
- materially stronger

- significantly harder to derail during coding

The package now feels:
- architected

instead of:
